rows.notes: 2025 PRODUCTION = DERIVED ESTIMATE, NOT COMPANY-REPORTED. CATL does not disclose mine output (CATL 2025 AR, 300750_2025.txt: no hits for 枧下窝 / 碳酸锂当量 / 锂精矿; the only lithium-mine mention is a tax-relief note for Yichun Times New Energy Mining, line 9155). Basis: (J1) an unnamed lithium analyst quoted by Daily Economic News says the three smelters tied to Jianxiawo ran at 7,000-8,500 t LCE/month in Q2 2025 and annual capacity is about 100,000 t LCE; (J2) a CITIC Futures analyst puts mine plus supporting smelters at about 10,000 t/month; search-result text (not opened) quotes a local partner at 5,000-6,000 t/month and a 2026 press item at 7,000-8,000 t/month before the halt. Calculation: mid-point 7,750 t/month x 7.26 months (1 Jan to the 9 Aug 2025 mining-right expiry/halt) = about 56,000 t LCE; the Q2 rate is assumed for Jan-Mar and July (J1 says July dipped slightly). Range across the quoted monthly rates is roughly 40,000-73,000 t LCE. Smelter output is used as the proxy for LCE mined; carbonate made from stockpiled ore after 9 Aug is not counted. Same chain as the refining row(s): do not sum with downstream carbonate. Context (search-result text, not opened): reserve report/renewal and a new safety permit 2026-06-29; Yichun EIA approval reported 2026-10-30 (Eastmoney snippet) after a brief informal restart in July 2026 per Benchmark snippet - restart not confirmed here, status/project_state unchanged. [lead] production is an ESTIMATE (analyst monthly run-rate × months to the 9 Aug 2025 halt); confidence 0.4; range 40–73 kt.

2025 production restated in LCE: 24,823 t = the company's lithium-battery-new-energy segment output, which Y3 shows is battery-grade lithium carbonate (sales 25,051 t, stock 225 t; 2024 output 26,048 t), made 'mainly from the company's own mine porcelain stone via an integrated mining-beneficiation-smelting chain' (Y2). It is carbonate leaving the plant, i.e. net of beneficiation and conversion losses, so it understates contained LCE mined, and some feed may come from other sources (AR calls Huaqiao Mining's Huashan the 'main guarantee channel', line 596). This SAME 24,823 t sits on the refining row yongxing-materials-yongxing-new-energy-lithium-carbonate-china (mining and refining are different steps: do not add them together as LCE supply). It REPLACES the earlier production of 3,000,000 t ore (company investor reply of 2026-09-12, SC003), which is kept in the SC003 note above and in installed_capacity; the ore figure could not be converted because the AR gives no average Li2O grade for the mined ore (only a >=0.20% Li2O cut-off, 410.0 Mt of 492.3 Mt ceramic clay; lines 594-596). production_norm cleared so the build converts from t LCE.

production_norm 18,815 t LCE = 126,800 t concentrate (table row 'concentrate, self-produced + toll-processed', 12.68 x 10,000 t, L1; SC120) x 6.0% Li2O x 2.473. THE 6.0% GRADE IS AN ASSUMPTION: neither Sichuan New Energy Power nor Yahua states the Lijiagou concentrate grade; 6% is the standard SC6 benchmark and the grade Rongjie quotes for its Jiajika concentrate (Rongjie 2025 AR). Sanity check: resource grade 1.29% Li2O on about 0.86 Mt of ore fed to the concentrator (1.0011 Mt mined less 142,900 t sold as ore) gives about 11 kt Li2O contained, so 126.8 kt x 6% = 7.6 kt Li2O is about 69% recovery during the ramp-up year - plausible. The earlier Mysteel 0.62% ore grade (SC003 note) is inconsistent with this output and is not used. Sensitivity: 5.5% gives 17,250 t; 7% (theoretical maximum, a 2024 Chinese mineral-processing paper cites 7.25%) gives 21,950 t. Production figure includes toll-processed concentrate.

Norm basis changed from t ore to CONTAINED t LCE in the ore (grade-based, before beneficiation losses): production_norm 19,121 t LCE = 577,000 t ROM ore mined in 2025 (G1) x 1.34% Li2O (average grade of the resource inside the mining right, G2; the mine-wide figure is 1.33%) x 2.473. capacity_norm 33,138 t LCE = 1,000,000 t/yr licensed ore scale x 1.34% x 2.473 (the pending 5 Mt/yr licence is not counted). The grade is the resource grade, not a measured run-of-mine feed grade, and the AR does not disclose concentrate output or recovery; recovered LCE in concentrate would be lower (for example about 15,000 t at 80% recovery - illustrative, not sourced). Production (577,000 t ore) and capacity (1,000,000 t ore) fields are unchanged. Guocheng holds only 48% (associate) - see SC120 ownership flag; the output is 100% of the mine.

2025 production 5,543 t Li2CO3 is DERIVED BY SUBTRACTION, not separately reported: Qinghai Salt Lake Industry produced 46,543 t Li2CO3 in 2025 (Q1) of which its Lanke Lithium subsidiary made 41,000 t (4.10 万吨, per its 48.58% shareholder Keda Manufacturing, Q2; rounding uncertainty about +/-50 t); the remainder is attributed to this 40,000 t/yr integrated project, which was built and fed for trial production only at end-September 2025 (Q3). Minmetals Salt Lake (Yiliping) was acquired only on 2026-01-31 and is not in the 2025 company output. Equals about 14% of nameplate over roughly one quarter of trial running, consistent with a start-up. The Mysteel note that Dec-2025 daily output was 60-70 t (SC003) is consistent in order of magnitude. Counted once: Lanke's 41,000 t is on the Lanke row.
